correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation of R=m y^2+(z-c)^2 gives 2my x(z-c)+2(z-c)(-b-mxy)=-2b(z-c). Integrating proves the finite-time mean formula. On bounded forward trajectories R(T)/T tends to zero; compact support justifies integrating the generator against an invariant probability measure. The Jacobian trace is exactly -z, so Liouville gives the determinant identity and the standard determinant/Oseledets relation gives Lyapunov-sum -c whenever the spectrum is defined. The periodic-orbit statement is the finite-time identity with R(T)=R(0).
